best_architecture: Decompose academic writing into a hierarchy of composable, skill-sized stages rather than a single monolithic prompt: outline -> section -> paragraph -> sentence, each implemented as an independent skill the agent can invoke and re-invoke. The dominant and most validated pattern is the two-stage 'pre-writing then writing' pipeline used by STORM (Stanford OVAL): (1) a pre-writing/research stage that gathers references and produces a structured outline, and (2) a writing stage that fills the outline section-by-section grounded in those references with inline citations. For papers specifically, the outline skill should target the IMRaD schema (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion/Conclusion) as a fixed scaffold, and section generation should run per-section (in canonical order: intro, background, methods, experimental setup, results, conclusion) as done in SakanaAI's AI Scientist, where each section is filled by a code-editing agent (Aider) given notes + figures, with an explicit instruction to use only real results and real citations to suppress hallucination. Key design decisions: (a) Separate concerns into distinct skills - outline generation, content drafting, style/tone transfer, summarization (Chain-of-Density), and citation validation - so each can be tested and improved independently. (b) Make citation/BibTeX validation a deterministic, non-LLM-first cascade (regex/BibTeX parse -> GROBID -> Crossref/arXiv DOI lookup, with LLM only as a fallback on messy entries) to minimize hallucinated references and token cost (RefChecker pattern). (c) Implement abstract/summary compression as an iterative Chain-of-Density loop (entity-sparse -> iteratively add salient entities at fixed length) rather than one-shot. (d) Implement tone normalization (casual -> formal academic) as a Text Style Transfer skill using in-context exemplars / style descriptors rather than fine-tuning, since prompt-based TST now matches or beats trained models and needs no data. (e) Treat the whole thing as a multi-agent / iterative-revision loop (draft -> reviewer feedback -> revise), mirroring ResearchAgent and the AI Scientist's automated reviewer, because single-pass long-form generation degrades in coherence. (f) Use a modular framework (STORM is built on DSPy) so each skill's prompt is a declarative, optimizable module rather than a brittle hardcoded string. The critical trade-off is grounding vs. fluency: every generative step must be tied to retrieved sources/real results, and citations must pass deterministic validation before the draft is considered done.
reference_papers: From Sparse to Dense: GPT-4 Summarization with Chain of Density Prompting (Adams et al. 2023) - arxiv:2309.04269 - the foundational Chain-of-Density paper; iterative entity-densification at fixed length; dataset on HuggingFace (griffin/chain_of_density); published at the 4th New Frontiers in Summarization Workshop (EMNLP 2023)

Assisting in Writing Wikipedia-like Articles From Scratch with Large Language Models (Shao et al. 2024, STORM) - arxiv:2402.14207 - two-stage pre-writing (outline via perspective-guided question asking + simulated conversation) then writing with citations; basis of stanford-oval/storm; NAACL 2024

Into the Unknown Unknowns: Engaged Human Learning through Participation in Language Model Agent Conversations (Jiang et al. 2024, Co-STORM) - arxiv:2408.15232 - collaborative discourse protocol with LLM-expert agents + a Moderator agent + dynamic mind-map knowledge base; human-in-the-loop steering; EMNLP 2024; the collaborative variant in stanford-oval/storm

The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery (Lu et al. 2024) - arxiv:2408.06292 - per-section LaTeX manuscript writing via Aider, Semantic Scholar citation retrieval (20 rounds), automated LLM peer-review loop; later published in Nature

LiRA: A Multi-Agent Framework for Reliable and Readable Literature Review Generation (2025) - arxiv:2510.05138 - explicit outline-drafting agent + specialized agents for writing, consistency refinement, and factual verification; directly relevant to outline->section decomposition

ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models (Baek et al. 2024) - arxiv:2404.07738 - multiple human-aligned ReviewingAgents giving feedback in an iterative revision loop; pattern for draft->review->revise

A Survey of Text Style Transfer: Applications and Ethical Implications (2024) - arxiv:2407.16737 - survey of TST including formality transfer; supports building tone normalization as an ensemble of formality/politeness/simplification transfers

Text Style Transfer Evaluation Using Large Language Models (Ostheimer et al. 2023) - arxiv:2308.13577 - zero-shot LLM prompting correlates strongly with human TST evaluation; prompt ensembling; relevant for evaluating casual->formal transfer

CiteAssist: A System for Automated Preprint Citation and BibTeX Generation (Kaesberg et al. 2024) - arxiv:2407.03192 - GROBID + PDF-LIB pipeline to extract and emit BibTeX (author/title/journal/volume/pages/year/DOI); reference for the citation-generation skill

pitfalls: Writing-skill failure modes the Gemma spec must defend against: (a) HALLUCINATED CITATIONS - the single most common and dangerous failure; the LLM invents plausible-sounding references with well-formatted but fake DOIs/titles/authors. Measured hallucination rates run 11-57% across deployed models. Mitigation: NEVER trust LLM-generated citation text; route every reference through the deterministic validation cascade (Crossref/arXiv/Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex DOI + title-identity lookup) BEFORE accepting it, and flag for human review on identifier conflict or low author-overlap (refchecker uses a <60% author-overlap threshold). (b) IMRaD SECTION-ORDERING DRIFT - the model muddles Methods content into Results, or Discussion into Conclusion; enforce a fixed section schema and canonical ordering constraint in the outline skill and validate the rendered structure against it. (c) SINGLE-PASS LONG-FORM DEGRADATION - coherence and citation grounding collapse after roughly 3000 tokens generated in one call; must split into per-section calls, never draft the whole paper in one shot (critical on a single A6000 with limited context budget). (d) TONE INCONSISTENCY ACROSS SECTIONS - sections drafted independently drift in register; run a Text Style Transfer unification pass over the assembled draft after all sections are written. (e) GROBID PDF-PARSE FAILURE on non-standard or scanned PDFs (corrupted/absent metadata, no DOI, arXiv-only) - need a fallback to scholarly/Semantic Scholar title search or manual entry rather than silently emitting garbage BibTeX. (f) BIBTEX KEY COLLISION - two papers by the same first author in the same year produce identical keys; must deduplicate (append a/b/c disambiguators). (g) ENTITY-SPARSE SUMMARIES from misapplied Chain-of-Density - the method must START sparse and iteratively densify; prompting it to 'start dense' produces unreadable, entity-jammed output. (h) ABSTRACT/WORD-COUNT OVERRUN - Chain-of-Density must hold a FIXED length each iteration (only entity density rises); without the fixed-length constraint the summary balloons. (i) RE-CITING / CONTRADICTING the same fact across sections because each section is drafted in isolation with no shared memory of what has already been asserted - track cited facts in a shared structure (see sota_improvements).
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: IMRaD outline generation
  Scenario: Outline skill produces a valid IMRaD scaffold
    Given a research topic and a set of gathered references
    When the outline skill is invoked
    Then the outline contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion/Conclusion sections
    And the sections are emitted in canonical IMRaD order
    And each section node carries the references assigned to it

Feature: Citation validation rejects hallucinated references
  Scenario: A fabricated reference is caught before acceptance
    Given a BibTeX entry whose DOI does not resolve and whose title is not found in Crossref, Semantic Scholar, or arXiv
    When the deterministic validation cascade runs
    Then the entry is marked invalid
    And it is flagged for human review rather than included in the bibliography
  Scenario: A real reference passes validation
    Given a BibTeX entry with a DOI that resolves to a matching title and author set
    When the validation cascade runs
    Then the entry is marked valid and added to references.bib with a unique citation key

Feature: Chain-of-Density abstract compression
  Scenario: Long abstract is compressed at fixed length with higher entity density
    Given an abstract text longer than 300 words
    When the Chain-of-Density skill is applied with a target of 150 words over 3 iterations
    Then the output is 150 words or fewer
    And the entity density of the output is greater than the entity density of the input
    And the word count does not increase across iterations

Feature: Section-by-section drafting
  Scenario: Each section is drafted in order with grounded citations
    Given a validated IMRaD outline with per-section references
    When the section-drafting skill is invoked for each section in canonical order
    Then each section contains inline citations that resolve to validated references
    And no section cites a reference that failed validation
    And the Results section reports only figures/numbers present in the supplied notes
sota_improvements: Beyond Gemma's original plan: (1) Co-STORM collaborative multi-perspective outlining (EMNLP 2024) instead of single-agent outlining - multiple LLM-expert personas plus a Moderator agent build a richer, less-blindspotted outline and maintain a dynamic mind-map knowledge base; adopt the mind-map as the shared fact store. (2) AI Scientist v2's template-free agentic tree-search drafting in place of a rigid fixed template, with a vision model giving feedback on figures - lets the structure adapt to the content rather than forcing every paper into one skeleton. (3) LLM-as-reviewer feedback loop: after a full draft, run an automated peer-review prompt (AI Scientist's reviewer / ResearchAgent's ReviewingAgents) and feed structured critiques back into a targeted revision pass, rather than accepting the first draft. (4) Knowledge graph / shared fact store tracking every cited fact across sections, so the writer never re-cites or contradicts a fact already asserted elsewhere (directly addresses pitfall (i)). (5) Retrieval-augmented per-section writing: run RAG over the local PDF library plus a live Semantic Scholar query for each section's reference gathering, so citations are grounded in retrieved passages instead of model memory. (6) Upgrade citation validation to the CiteCheck three-class severity scheme (exact match / minor metadata corruption / full fabrication) rather than binary valid/invalid, so minor metadata drift (year off by one, venue variation) is auto-corrected while fabrications are hard-blocked and flagged.
